lit.'<p>Al aumentar la población, el aliment:
'

As the population grows, food and space per individual decrease: births fall and deaths rise. These are density-dependent factors. The population grows in an S shape (logistic growth) and levels off at the carrying capacity K: the maximum the environment can sustain. Other factors, such as a frost or a fire, act regardless of density.

'
lit.'<p>Las actividades humanas cambian los:
'

Human activities change ecosystems: habitat loss (urban growth, fires, monocultures) reduces carrying capacity; hunting predators can trigger herbivore explosions; pollution and climate change affect births and deaths. Protected areas and the control of invasive species help conserve biodiversity.

'
lit.'<p>Llegan los <b>zorros culpeo</b>. Con:
'

Culpeo foxes arrive. With plenty of prey, the predators feed well and breed; as they increase, they eat more degus and these decline; then, short of food, the foxes decline and the degus recover. The two populations oscillate, with the predator peak after the prey peak. Predation regulates both populations.

'
lit.'<p>Se introduce el <b>conejo europeo</b:
'

The European rabbit is introduced; it eats the same grasses as the degu: there is interspecific competition. The rabbit, with no effective natural enemies in Chile, breeds faster and displaces the degu. Invasive species are one of the main causes of biodiversity loss. Other interactions are mutualism (both benefit, like bees and flowers) and parasitism.

'
lit.'<p>Si hay alimento y espacio de sobra y:
'

If food and space are plentiful and there are no predators, each generation is larger than the last by the same proportion: growth is exponential (a J-shaped curve), dN/dt = r·N. No population can grow like this for long: resources run out. It happens when a new environment is colonised, like the European rabbit on arriving in Chile.

'
lit.'<p>Un <b>individuo</b> es un organismo,:
'

An individual is a single organism, such as a degu. The degus of one place form a population (same species, same place and time). The populations of different species living together —grasses, degus, culpeo foxes— form a community. The community together with the abiotic factors (water, light, temperature, soil) is an ecosystem, such as the scrubland of central Chile.

'
